newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkey to tender for $2-billion thermal plant.
newsitem.headline: Turkey to tender for $2-billion thermal plant.

text.p: Turkey, facing power shortages, will invite tenders for a thermal power plant in the country's east which will cost about $2 billion and produce eight billion kiloWatt-hours (kWh) of power a year, Anatolian news agency said on Friday.

"About $2 billion dollars will be invested for the power plant which will produce eight billion kWh a year," Afif Demirkiran, general manager of state power producer TEAS, was quoted by the agency as saying.
"The tender will be put out in two months and the plans will have four power generation units," he said.
He said the plant would be similar in output capacity and size with an existing one operating in the Afsin-Elbistan region, near Kahramanmaras in eastern Turkey.
He said the region had lignite coal reserves of 3.5 billion tonnes -- half Turkey's total lignite capacity -- which can supply three more plants that can totally produce up to 50 billion kWh a year.
Turkey this week opened tenders for 11 small-size power plants to which local contractors were invited. Energy officials said they planned 44 other tenders for other small-size plants in 1997.

Turkey's power demand growth is estimated to hit 12 percent this year, against eight percent predicted earlier, and the country began electricity imports from Iran in August to make up for a supply shortfall of about four billion kWh this year.
